Now, by \cref{prop:recurrence}, there exists \as a subsequence $\score_{\run_{\runalt}}$ of $\score_{\run}$ and some (possibly random) $\sol\in\sols$ such that $\lim_{\runalt\to\infty} \fench(\sol,\score_{\run_{\runalt}}) = 0$.
Since the limit $\lim_{\run\to\infty} \fench(\sol,\score_{\run})$ exists \as, it follows that $\lim_{\run\to\infty} \fench(\sol,\score_{\run}) = 0$.
This shows that, with probability $1$, $\act_{\run} = \mirror(\score_{\run})$ converges to some (random) minimum point $\sol$ of \eqref{eq:opt}, as claimed.

To establish this claim, assume instead that there is no $\eps$-ball $\ball(\sols,\eps)$ contained in $\fball(\sols, \delta)$.
Then, for all $\runalt>0$ there exists some $\dstate_{\runalt}\in\dstates$ such that $\dist(\sols,\mirror(\dstate_{\runalt})) = 1/\runalt$ but $\fench(\sols, y_{\delta}) \geq \eps$.
This produces a sequence $(\dstate_{\runalt})_{\runalt=1}^{\infty}$ such that $\dist(\sols,\mirror(\dstate_{\runalt})) \to 0$ but $\fench(\sols, \dstate_{\runalt}) \geq \eps$.
Since $\states$ is compact and $\sols$ is closed, we can assume without loss of generality that $\mirror(\dstate_{\runalt})\to\base$ for some $\base\in\sols$ (at worst, we only need to descend to a subsequence of $\dstate_{\runalt}$).
We thus get
\begin{equation}
\eps
	\leq \fench(\sols,\dstate_{\runalt})
	\leq \fench(\base,\dstate_{\runalt}).
\end{equation}
However, since $\mirror(\dstate_{\runalt})\to\base$, \cref{asm:reciprocity} gives $\fench(\base,\dstate_{\runalt})\to0$, a contradiction.
We conclude that $\fball(\sols,\delta)$ contains an $\eps$-neighborhood of $\sols$, as required.
\end{proofstep}
\end{proofof}

nodes.title: 凸次梯度最优性
declaration_text: For a proper closed convex regularizer h extended by +infinity outside its domain, x maximizes <y,x>-h(x) exactly when y belongs to the convex subdifferential of h at x. When h* is differentiable, its gradient equals this unique maximizer. These are the convex-analysis facts cited to Roc70.

nodes.title: 强凸共轭光滑性与双共轭
declaration_text: A proper lower-semicontinuous convex function equals its biconjugate. If h is K-strongly convex, h* is differentiable and satisfies h*(y') <= h*(y)+<grad h*(y),y'-y>+||y'-y||_*^2/(2K). The author cites RW98, Theorems 11.1 and 12.60.

nodes.title: 鞅差强大数律
declaration_text: For a martingale M_n=sum_{k=1}^n d_k and deterministic nondecreasing positive tau_n tending to infinity, if sum_n tau_n^(-p) E[|d_n|^p | F_{n-1}] is finite almost surely for some p in [1,2], then M_n/tau_n tends to zero almost surely. This is the standard theorem stated in B0145 and attributed to HH80.

nodes.title: Doob次鞅收敛定理
declaration_text: An L1-bounded submartingale converges almost surely to an integrable random variable. This is the standard theorem stated in B0147 and attributed to HH80.

nodes.title: Gladyshev收敛引理
declaration_text: If nonnegative random variables a_n satisfy E[a_{n+1}|a_1,...,a_n] <= (1+delta_n)a_n+epsilon_n for nonnegative deterministic summable sequences delta_n and epsilon_n, then a_n converges almost surely to a finite nonnegative random variable. This is B0072, attributed to Pol87, p. 49.

nodes.title: 期望交换与条件期望基本性质
declaration_text: Dominated convergence permits differentiation under expectation when its domination hypotheses hold. Jensen's inequality bounds the squared norm of an expectation by the expectation of the squared norm. Independence of a fresh sample from the past permits conditional averaging at a predictable state, and predictable factors can be taken outside conditional expectations.
